font.b: Feedback Propagation in a Solver-Critic LLM System

div.b: What internal representations change when an LLM solver accepts or rejects critic feedback, and are those representations causally involved in feedback uptake?

div.div: Original multi-hop QA questions (2–4 hops) with supporting and distractor paragraphs

ul.li: MuSiQue-style 2-, 3- and 4-hop questions, one supporting paragraph per hop
Related distractor and filler paragraphs (20 paragraphs per question)
Structural validation and deduplication against MuSiQue

div.div: Split by question family into train / validation / test, plus a held-out intervention set

div.b: Solver–Critic Interaction Dataset: Natural Condition Only (no forced feedback)
div.div: The Critic never sees the gold answer and is not told what to argue; whether its feedback is right or wrong arises naturally
Gemma 3 4B IT answers from the paragraphs
Qwen3 4B answers blind, then compares with the Solver and recommends an answer
Sees both answers as Candidate A / B (order balanced) and answers again
Labels each attempt-2 answer: Adoption / Retention / Agreement / Out
Adoption vs. Retention episodes are the probe target
Compare validation balanced accuracy / AUROC across candidate layers → Layer 25
On Layer 25 activations: custom L1 SAE, Gemma Scope pretrained SAE, decoder-adapted SAE
Linear probe on SAE features; select the top 10 Adoption and top 10 Retention features
Steer selected feature directions during attempt 2 (increase / decrease / both, fixed size); compare with equal-size random features

ul.li: Behavioral: counts of the four Claude labels (Adoption / Retention / Agreement / Out)
Probe: prediction performance (balanced accuracy / AUROC) on held-out data
Causal: decision flip rate for targeted vs. random edits (Holm-corrected), with Out answers reported separately as broken outputs
